name: Pompeii
desc: A whole Roman city paused mid-bite by Vesuvius — streets, bakeries, 2,000-year-old graffiti fresher than your feed.

name: Mount Vesuvius
desc: Peer into the crater that made Pompeii famous. Still technically awake, which makes the hike deliciously dramatic.

name: National Archaeological Museum
desc: Where Pompeii's best stuff actually lives — mosaics, bronzes, and one room the Victorians deemed too spicy.

name: Spaccanapoli
desc: The straight-line street that slices old Naples in two. Laundry overhead, scooters everywhere, drama included free.

name: Castel dell'Ovo
desc: A sea castle allegedly balanced on a magic egg. If the egg breaks, Naples falls. No pressure. Bay views: free.

name: Galleria Umberto I
desc: A glass-domed shopping cathedral where doing absolutely nothing feels expensive. It isn't.

name: Napoli Sotterranea
desc: Forty meters under the pizza: Greek-Roman tunnels and WWII shelters. Bring curiosity, leave claustrophobia at street level.

name: Piazza del Plebiscito
desc: A vast stone stage where kids play football between royal colonnades. Naples' living room, no cover charge.

name: Lungomare Caracciolo
desc: Sunset seafront stroll with Vesuvius posing across the bay. The whole postcard, zero euros.

name: San Gregorio Armeno
desc: The alley where artisans carve tiny popes and footballers for nativity scenes all year. Christmas never checks out here.
